key_insight: The paper presents a matrix-free finite-element Bayesian uncertainty quantification framework for 3D photoacoustic tomography that enables scalable posterior sampling with accurate adjoint-consistent wave discretization.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical route to quantify reconstruction uncertainty in realistic 3D PAT geometries, which is important for biomedical imaging reliability and for extending Bayesian inverse methods to other PDE-constrained problems.
method: Reformulate randomize-then-optimize (RTO) as a matrix-free sampler using forward and adjoint wave solves.
Construct an adjoint discretization that is an exact transpose of the discrete forward operator and remains consistent with the continuous adjoint.
Study temporal discretization and artificial boundary conditions to avoid numerical artifacts in posterior uncertainty.
evidence_signal: The approach is validated against exact posterior statistics, existing Bayesian PAT methods, and NUTS, and demonstrated on a 3D finite-element case with about 2×10^5 unknowns.
watch_item: Performance and posterior accuracy depend on careful adjoint consistency and discretization choices, so mismatched forward/adjoint implementations or boundary treatments can introduce artifacts.
paper_title: 3D Uncertainty Quantification for the Photo-Acoustic Tomography
